purpose: Separate AVF acquisition/provider state from host capability, restricted permissions, real guest boot evidence and platform fallback. Source presence or successful acquisition MUST NOT imply guest boot.

G1_TRANSPORT_PROVIDER.pass: Canonical source acquired through an authorized compatible transport with immutable provenance and read-back.
G1_TRANSPORT_PROVIDER.blocked: Provider/special-file/destination incompatibility remains typed and preserved; no mirror substitution or source sanitization inside probe.

G2_HOST_CAPABILITY.pass_android: API >=34 AND VirtualMachineManager available (or virtualization framework system feature present) AND at least one protected/non-protected capability bit is set.
G2_HOST_CAPABILITY.blocked_android: Manager absent and feature absent, API below supported surface, or both capability bits false.
G2_HOST_CAPABILITY.non_android: NOT_APPLICABLE for AVF; select platform backend/fallback instead.

G3_PERMISSION.pass: MANAGE_VIRTUAL_MACHINE is actually granted for AVF API use; USE_CUSTOM_VIRTUAL_MACHINE additionally required only for custom-VM path that needs it.
G3_PERMISSION.blocked: Restricted permission not granted. Ordinary third-party APK must not be assumed to possess it.

G4_GUEST_BOOT_EVIDENCE.pass: A real VM was created/started on the target host and evidence contains run/log/artifact reference plus strong hash/read-back.
G4_GUEST_BOOT_EVIDENCE.blocked: NOT_RUN or FAIL. Source presence, provider acquisition, API availability and capability bits alone never satisfy this gate.

G5_PLATFORM_FALLBACK.rule: Fallback is selected only after preceding capability/permission result; fallback does not convert an AVF GAP into AVF PASS.
G5_PLATFORM_FALLBACK.android: AVF/crosvm first when gates pass; otherwise QEMU-compatible fallback if implemented/authorized.
G5_PLATFORM_FALLBACK.ios_ipados: QEMU/UTM-style path subject to Apple/JIT restrictions; AVF NOT_APPLICABLE.
G5_PLATFORM_FALLBACK.web: No native AVF claim; browser/PWA layer cannot claim local AVF guest boot without a separate supported runtime backend.

Android_ARM64_physical.fallback: QEMU-compatible backend only if separately implemented and verified

Web_browser_PWA.preferred_backend: UI/control surface only unless a separately supported runtime is provided

normalized_probe_output.selected_backend: AVF_PROTECTED | AVF_NON_PROTECTED | KVM_QEMU | WHPX_QEMU | QEMU_FALLBACK | IOS_QEMU_STYLE | NONE
normalized_probe_output.overall: READY_FOR_RUNTIME_TEST | BLOCKED_PROVIDER | BLOCKED_CAPABILITY | BLOCKED_PERMISSION | BLOCKED_GUEST_BOOT | FALLBACK_SELECTED | UNSUPPORTED

evidence_anchors.official_virtual_machine_manager: android.googlesource.com platform/packages/modules/Virtualization javalib VirtualMachineManager.java: getCapabilities(), CAPABILITY_PROTECTED_VM=1, CAPABILITY_NON_PROTECTED_VM=2
evidence_anchors.official_avf_api_readme: android.googlesource.com platform/packages/modules/Virtualization/javalib README: SystemApi, API 34+, restricted MANAGE_VIRTUAL_MACHINE, feature detection
evidence_anchors.functional_project_rule: Virtual Computer source document: Android AVF/crosvm first, QEMU fallback; Linux/Windows use distinct backends; real local VM boot required
evidence_anchors.memory_audit_rule: Workflow/Memory source document: evidence/state/checkpoint must be persisted; source presence is not equivalent to validated global completion

refutations: REFUTE: AVF source exists therefore AVF works on the host.
REFUTE: successful provider acquisition therefore a VM can boot.
REFUTE: VirtualMachineManager presence therefore required permissions are granted.
REFUTE: Android AVF capability implies Linux/Windows/iOS/Web AVF support.
REFUTE: fallback success may be reported as AVF success.
